summary: Fail on one kept blocker. B1, N1, N2, TS1, LC1 from review-b-cc8afbd are fixed and withdrawn: quota.ts:68,291 reads the week window under the live key `weekly`; the live GET at 127.0.0.1:38307 printed state ready with windows 5h 5.15, weekly 2.06, monthly 1.03; Q11 pins wait at weekly 100; Q15 pins stopped when the 5h or weekly name is absent; both runners key IS_GO_ROUTE on quota_provider (review-run.sh:261, judge-run.sh:245), the same field quota.ts reads; all fakes emit the live key set. Gates: quota 24 passed (24), review-run 53 pass 0 fail (bun), judge-run 30 passed (30). The drivers night-4.11.sh and probe-4.10.sh fail closed: a missing 5h or weekly key raises and prints fail, so the route is skipped. The 80 % stop holds for non-Go routes (review-run.sh:786-789, judge-run.sh:692), and a non-Go route cannot take the Go thresholds because the provider comes from the repo-owned routes.json row and the quota answer cannot set it. Kept blocker: B2 is only half closed. quota.ts:319-324 checks the window NAMES, not the usable values, so a present-but-unusable weekly (null, string, or negative) beside a usable 5h gives ready. Q13 (quota.test.ts:626-674) pins exactly this: {5h:50, weekly:-1, monthly:10} -> ready, and I reproduced it inline against quota.ts (state ready). This is fail-open on the Go week threshold: when the weekly value cannot be evaluated, the gate that protects real Go spend starts a pass, probe, or judge call anyway. Plan row 4.13j states B2 as 'both 5h and weekly must be finite numbers, else stopped', and spec D15 defines unusable windows as skipped and a Go answer lacking 5h or weekly as stopped. A2 and A6 do not apply.
blocking_findings: B2 [Blocker] harness/model-guide/quota.ts:319-324 (with stateOf :288-297): the required-window rule checks answer.names (every name of the answer, usable or not), not the usable windows map. So a present-but-unusable weekly beside a usable 5h gives ready. Evidence: Q13 (harness/model-guide-tests/quota.test.ts:648-662) pins {5h:50, weekly:-1, monthly:10} -> ready and passed in gate 1; my inline probe against quota.ts with the same body printed {"provider":"opencode-go","source":"opencode-go","state":"ready","cap":3,"windows":{"5h":50,"monthly":10}}. A weekly with a wrong shape (weekly:{percent:50}) or a null weekly after a schema drift takes the same path: the name is present, the value is skipped, and the Go 100 % week threshold never fires. Plan row 4.13j states B2 as 'both 5h and weekly must be finite numbers, else stopped'; spec D15 skips unusable windows and gives stopped for a Go answer that lacks the 5h or the weekly window. Effect: a damaged or drifted Go quota answer starts a pass, probe, or judge call with unknown week usage (fail open on the PM-order threshold). Fix: for opencode-go, require usable values (finite numbers, not negative) for both 5h and weekly from the usable windows map; if either is absent there, return stopped. Q13 changes to match: usable 5h with a negative, string, null, or wrong-shape weekly gives stopped; the only-string case stays stopped. Q12 stays as-is (a null credits_balance beside usable windows is not a required window). | CONTEST kept: Green implemented a name-presence check and pinned the fail-open as Q13 ready; the plan row's own B2 text requires finite numbers else stopped, and a spend gate must fail closed when the weekly value cannot be evaluated.
nonblocking_findings: ND1 [Minor] The night drivers accept a negative usedPercent. night-4.11.sh:80-88 and probe-4.10.sh:65-73 test usable(value) only for int/float, so weekly -1 passes and stop stays 0; the route proceeds. The runners re-check through quota.ts before each call, so real spend is still gated, and the live endpoint emits real percentages. Fix: reject value < 0 in usable() in both drivers so the pre-flight gate matches quota.ts.

After gate 1 the pgrep scans showed one transient fake-opencode pair and quota-server under /tmp/mg-review-run-2OPVN6 and /tmp/mg-review-fake-q69Hvg; after gate 2 one quota-server under /tmp/mg-judge-fake-AAlWIQ; after gate 3 one under /tmp/mg-review-fake-ZjN8UL. I started and killed one inline probe server on 127.0.0.1:18653 only.

B2 reproduction: a background inline node server on 127.0.0.1:18653 returned {usage:{windows:{5h:{usedPercent:50},weekly:{usedPercent:-1},monthly:{usedPercent:10}}}}; npx tsx model-guide/quota.ts --provider opencode-go --base http://127.0.0.1:18653 printed state ready with windows {5h:50, monthly:10} and exit 0. quota.ts:319-324 checks answer.names, which holds every name, so the skipped weekly passes the check.

Drivers fail closed on the same rule: night-4.11.sh:74-75 and probe-4.10.sh:59-60 read windows['5h'] and windows['weekly']; a missing key raises and prints fail (night-4.11.sh:76-78, probe-4.10.sh:61-63), and a non-usable value prints fail (:83-85, :68-70), so the route is skipped (:137-144, :111-118). Both drivers gate only opencode-go/* routes by route prefix.

Non-Go isolation: QUOTA_PROVIDER comes from the repo-owned routes.json row for the --route value; the quota answer cannot set the provider, and a row with quota_provider opencode-go is a Go route by definition. The 80 % stop for other sources holds at review-run.sh:786-789 and judge-run.sh:692 (IS_GO_ROUTE != 1).
